title: Direct the giggle before you write the script
description: A baby-voice segment lives or dies in the first ten seconds: script length, giggle placement and pacing decide whether it reads as a character or a demo.

prompts.label: Quick test
prompts.prompt:
Act as an audio producer cutting a 30-second baby-voice intro for a parenting podcast. Direct the performance before you generate a single line.

Inputs [replace]: host line 'Welcome back to Small Hours'; baby character 'Pip'; three approved giggle moments; delivery WAV 48 kHz, 24-bit, mono.

Deliverable: one 30s WAV at 48 kHz plus one 10s hook cut, a script sheet with timecodes, and a take log.

Design system: hook line inside 3s; giggles at 6s, 17s and 26s; 250 ms pause after each giggle; one pitch register; no line longer than 12 words.

Workflow: 1) restate the script and count syllables per line; 2) cut anything that cannot fit 30s; 3) mark giggle and pause timecodes; 4) generate the voice in one register; 5) check the first 10s without video; 6) run gates; 7) export both cuts.

Gates: no adult phonemes in baby lines; each giggle within 200 ms of its mark; no line over 12 words; loudness -16 LUFS; total length within 0.5s of 30s.

Audit: the lines you cut, the giggle that drifted, and whether the first 10s still works without the host.

Do not add a sponsor or claim; do not pitch the voice up as a shortcut; do not reuse one giggle three times.

prompts.label: Production
prompts.prompt:
Act as a senior audio producer building a three-minute bedtime-story segment in one baby voice, with two characters and a repeatable pacing system.

Inputs [replace]: story brief 'Pip and the paper boat'; 420-word script; two characters (Pip, Nan); four cues (water, paper, yawn, page turn); delivery WAV 48 kHz/24-bit plus MP3 320 kbps.

Deliverables: one 3:00 master, one 60s trailer, stems per character, a timecode script, and a cue sheet; names episode-version.

Design system: 8-12 words per line; 300 ms pause at scene changes; giggle only at three marked beats; music bed -24 LUFS under voice; voice -16 LUFS; no line over 4s.

Workflow: 1) intake the script and mark scene beats; 2) cut to 3:00 and log the cuts; 3) assign lines to characters; 4) record each character in one register; 5) place cues and pauses; 6) check the first and last 10s; 7) run gates; 8) export master, trailer and stems.

Cue sheet lists the exact in and out timecode per cue.

Gates: no line over 12 words; cues within 150 ms; voice and bed at target loudness; no character drift between scenes; total 3:00 plus or minus 2s; no invented story beat.

Audit: cuts, character drift, cue timing, and the beat most likely to fail on re-listen.

Do not add narration I did not write; do not change the ending; do not stack two giggle samples.

prompts.label: Edge / stress
prompts.prompt:
Act as an audio producer stress-testing a baby-voice read when the script is too long for the slot.

Inputs [replace]: 68-word sentence for a 10-second slot; three required product-neutral phrases; one giggle mark at 4s; delivery 48 kHz WAV.

Deliverable: one 10s cut, one 14s alternate, a fit report, and a clip list.

Design system: 8-11 words per line; giggle at 4s; no line over 4s; voice in one register.

Workflow: 1) count syllables and estimate read time at the target pace; 2) list what can be cut without changing meaning; 3) try the 10s cut and measure overrun; 4) if overrun exceeds 1s, deliver the 14s alternate; 5) keep the giggle mark; 6) run gates; 7) export with the fit report.

Gates: overrun reported in seconds; no phrase cut mid-word; giggle on the mark; no speed-up above 8%; loudness -16 LUFS.

Audit: the overrun, the cut version you refused, and whether the 10s slot needs a script rewrite.

Do not chipmunk the voice to fit; do not drop a required phrase silently; do not claim the 10s cut works when it overruns.

title: One thumbnail brief, four sizes, one type hierarchy
description: The same idea has to survive 1:1, 16:9, 9:16 and print: lock the crop and the type scale before generating four files.

prompts.label: Quick test
prompts.prompt:
Act as a thumbnail art director producing one video thumbnail in four sizes from a single brief.

Inputs [replace]: video title 'I rebuilt a 1970s camper in 30 days'; 3000 px photo of a man beside the camper; palette rust #B4553C, cream #F2E9DA, ink #1F1B18; four-word hook '30 days. One camper.'

Deliverable: four PNGs at 1280x720, 1080x1080, 1080x1920 and a 300 dpi print PDF; one type-scale sheet.

Design system: hook type at 12% of frame height; face 28-34%; safe margin 6%; three words per line maximum; one accent; no gradient behind type.

Workflow: 1) restate the idea in four words; 2) define the crop box per ratio; 3) set one type scale and one accent; 4) generate the 16:9 first; 5) crop the other three from the same master; 6) check at 20% size; 7) run gates; 8) export.

Gates: hook spelled exactly; face not cropped at the chin; type legible at 20%; safe margin respected; no extra text.

Audit: the ratio that lost the subject, the type size you changed, and the crop that needs a reshoot.

Do not add arrows or circles I did not ask for; do not stretch the face; do not add a second accent.

prompts.label: Production
prompts.prompt:
Act as a thumbnail lead building a ten-video series system where every episode keeps one type hierarchy across four sizes.

Inputs [replace]: ten episode titles, ten subject photos, one host portrait, palette rust #B4553C, cream #F2E9DA, ink #1F1B18; delivery 1280x720, 1080x1080, 1080x1920 and 300 dpi print PDF.

Deliverables: forty files, a type-scale sheet, a crop map per episode, and a naming system episode-ratio-version.

Design system: hook 10-12% of frame height; face 26-34%; safe margin 6%; two type sizes only; one accent per episode; text block never over the face. The crop map lists the exact pixel crop per ratio.

Workflow: 1) intake titles and cut each to four words; 2) lock the type scale and crop map; 3) build episode one as canary; 4) review at 20% and full size; 5) batch the remaining nine; 6) check the series wall; 7) run gates; 8) export with the crop map.

Gates: every hook exact; no face cropped at chin or eye line; type legible at 20%; series uses two type sizes; forty files at correct dimensions; no episode repeats another composition.

Audit: the episodes that broke the scale, the crops that needed a new photo, and the pair that looks too similar.

Do not rotate one composition across ten episodes; do not add stickers or emoji; do not change the host's face.

prompts.label: Edge / stress
prompts.prompt:
Act as a thumbnail director stress-testing a long title and a busy source photo.

Inputs [replace]: 18-word title, 1600 px phone photo with a cluttered workshop behind the subject, low subject-background contrast; palette ink #1F1B18 and rust #B4553C.

Deliverable: three 1280x720 options, one 1080x1920 cut, a legibility report at 20%, and a crop note.

Design system: hook 12% of frame height; safe margin 6%.

Workflow: 1) cut the title to three options of four words or fewer; 2) separate subject from background; 3) test type over the busiest area; 4) check at 20% size and at 120 px width; 5) keep only options that read at both; 6) run gates; 7) export with the report.

Gates: no option exceeds four words; subject edge clean at 100%; contrast at least 4.5:1 for type; no text over the face; no invented prop.

Audit: the title you cut, the option that failed at 20%, and whether the photo needs a reshoot.

Do not blur the background into a fake studio; do not outline every letter; do not ship an option that only reads at full size.

title: Plan the export budget before the fifth image
description: A five-file daily cap turns generation into a queue: lock the style and the aspect ratios first, so every download is a keeper.

prompts.label: Quick test
prompts.prompt:
Act as a brand designer producing a five-image set that must be worth every download.

Inputs [replace]: theme 'coastal morning' for a skincare brand; palette sand #D8C3A5, sea #7A9E9F, ink #1F1B18; five subjects (bottle, texture, hands, shoreline, flat lay); export 3840x2160 PNG.

Deliverable: five 4K PNGs, one contact sheet at 2400 px, and a style spec with three locked fields.

Design system: one camera height; one light direction; one grade; subject 35-55% of frame; no text inside the image; grain 1.5%.

Workflow: 1) write a five-field style spec; 2) generate one test frame and check at 100%; 3) lock seed, light and grade; 4) generate the five subjects; 5) reject any frame that breaks the spec; 6) run gates; 7) export five files and the contact sheet.

Gates: all five at 3840x2160; one light direction; palette within 3%; no watermark; no invented label text.

Audit: frames rejected against the cap, the field that drifted, and which image you would replace first.

Do not spend a download on a frame that fails the spec; do not add text; do not change grade mid-set.

prompts.label: Production
prompts.prompt:
Act as an art director planning a twenty-image campaign around a five-file daily export cap.

Inputs [replace]: campaign 'linen at home'; four subjects (bed, chair, table, curtain) with five crops each; palette oat #E8DCCB, clay #B4553C, ink #1F1B18; export 3840x2160 PNG plus 1080x1350 JPEG.

Deliverables: twenty 4K masters and twenty 1080x1350 crops at 300 dpi across four days, a day plan, a style spec, and a contact sheet per day; names subject-crop-day.

Design system: one light direction per day; subject 30-50%; grade locked on day one; grain 1.5%; no text; crop safe margin 8%.

Workflow: 1) intake the twenty-frame list and rank by value; 2) write the style spec; 3) map frames to a four-day plan, five per day; 4) canary one frame per subject; 5) check at 100% and reject failures; 6) generate the rest on plan; 7) run gates; 8) export with the day plan.

Gates: exactly five exports per day; all masters 4K; one light direction per day; palette within 3%; no duplicate composition; no invented product detail.

Audit: the frames you deferred, the day that hit the cap early, and the crop most likely to be replaced.

Do not exceed the daily cap and then call the set complete; do not reuse one frame at two crops without saying so; do not change grade between days.

prompts.label: Edge / stress
prompts.prompt:
Act as a designer stress-testing an export plan when the last download fails.

Inputs [replace]: four approved 4K frames, one failed export at 92% progress, a client deadline in 2 hours, one alternate crop ready; palette and grade locked.

Deliverable: a recovery plan, the best four-file set, one 1920x1080 fallback marked as such, and an incident note.

Design system: grade locked; no crop below 1080 px; 300 dpi on approved files.

Workflow: 1) list what is approved, exported and missing; 2) rank remaining frames by campaign value; 3) retry once and record the failure point; 4) if it fails again, promote the alternate crop; 5) mark any fallback resolution honestly; 6) run gates; 7) export with the note.

Gates: no frame passed off as 4K if it is not; failure point recorded; alternate crop meets the grade; no missing file hidden; delivery list matches files.

Audit: what failed, what you substituted, and whether the deadline forces a lower resolution.

Do not fake a 4K file by upscaling silently; do not skip the failure note; do not deliver five files when only four exist.

title: Design for the distance, not the canvas
description: A window sign, a shelf talker and an end cap are read at 8 m, 1 m and 2 m; set the type size from the viewing distance before layout.

prompts.label: Quick test
prompts.prompt:
Act as a retail graphic designer producing one promo in two display types: a window poster and a shelf talker.

Inputs [replace]: promo 'Summer refill week, 20% off'; store 'Marche & Co'; palette olive #5B6B4A, cream #F2E9DA, ink #1F1B18; 3000 px product photo of a refill bottle.

Deliverable: one A2 window poster at 300 dpi PDF with 3 mm bleed, one A6 shelf talker at 300 dpi, and a distance test note.

Design system: window headline readable at 8 m (90 mm cap height minimum); shelf price readable at 1 m (12 mm minimum); safe margin 8 mm; two type sizes; one accent; no more than 12 words per sign.

Workflow: 1) restate promo and price; 2) set reading distances; 3) choose type sizes from distance; 4) lay out the window first; 5) adapt to the shelf talker; 6) check at 1:10 and 1:1; 7) run gates; 8) export both with bleed.

Gates: price spelled exactly; headline 90 mm minimum at A2; shelf price 12 mm minimum; 3 mm bleed; no unapproved claim; no text over the product.

Audit: the distance you sized for, the line you cut, and the sign that needs a bigger format.

Do not add a discount I did not approve; do not stretch the logo; do not put 40 words on a shelf talker.

prompts.label: Production
prompts.prompt:
Act as a retail design lead building eight display types for one promotion across three store sizes.

Inputs [replace]: promo 'Back to school, 15% off'; three stores (flagship 12 m window, high street 6 m, mall kiosk); palette navy #1F2A44, chalk #F5F1E8, orange #D96B2B; product cut-outs and approved copy.

Deliverables: eight display types (window poster, hanging banner, shelf talker, end cap, floor decal, wobbler, A-frame, counter card) as print-ready PDFs at 300 dpi with 3 mm bleed; a distance map; names display-store-version.

Design system: type sized by distance (window 90 mm+, shelf 12 mm+, end cap 40 mm+); 8 mm safe margin; two type sizes plus price; one accent; no more than 12 words per sign.

Workflow: 1) intake promo, prices and store sizes; 2) build a distance map; 3) set the type scale; 4) design the flagship window first; 5) adapt to the other seven types; 6) test all eight at 1:10; 7) run gates; 8) export with the distance map.

Gates: every price exact; every display 300 dpi with 3 mm bleed; type meets distance minimum; no sign over 12 words; logo unaltered; no invented offer.

Audit: the display that lost readability, the store that needs a different format, and the sign you would reprint.

Do not reuse the window layout at shelf size; do not add a second offer; do not change brand colors per store.

prompts.label: Edge / stress
prompts.prompt:
Act as a retail designer stress-testing a price change after files are print-ready.

Inputs [replace]: six print-ready PDFs for '20% off', price change to '15% off' approved 30 minutes before print, one sign already printed; palette olive #5B6B4A, cream #F2E9DA.

Deliverable: six revised PDFs, a change log, a reprint list, and a note on the printed sign.

Design system: price 12 mm minimum; 3 mm bleed; 300 dpi.

Workflow: 1) list every file and the text box holding the price; 2) change the number only, not the layout; 3) check every instance at 1:1; 4) mark which files need reprint; 5) flag the printed sign for sticker or reprint; 6) run gates; 7) export with the change log.

Gates: price exact in all six; no layout shift beyond 1 mm; no old price left visible; bleed intact; printed sign documented.

Audit: files changed, files reprinted, and whether the printed sign can be patched.

Do not redesign the layout to hide the change; do not leave an old price in a corner; do not say the printed sign is fixed when it is not.

title: Three dead zones decide the header
description: The 1500x500 banner is cropped by the avatar, the display name and the mobile view; place the message where none of them lands.

prompts.label: Quick test
prompts.prompt:
Act as a social art director designing one X/Twitter header with the platform's dead zones marked first.

Inputs [replace]: account 'Field Notes Studio'; tagline 'Slow travel, printed monthly'; palette forest #2F4A3C, paper #F2E9DA, ink #1F1B18; 3000 px photo of a mountain road.

Deliverable: one 1500x500 PNG, one mobile crop proof at 600x200, and a safe-zone overlay.

Design system: logo 90x90 px inside the left 120 px; tagline baseline at 70% height; safe area 60% of width; type 28 px minimum; avatar dead zone left 150 px; mobile crop keeps the center 600 px.

Workflow: 1) mark avatar, name and mobile dead zones; 2) place logo and tagline outside them; 3) set type at 28 px minimum; 4) generate the background; 5) check the mobile crop; 6) run gates; 7) export with the overlay.

Gates: logo not under the avatar; tagline visible at 600x200; no text in the top 40 px; contrast 4.5:1; exact 1500x500.

Audit: the zone that ate the tagline, the crop you changed, and the element you moved.

Do not center the logo; do not add a second tagline; do not use type smaller than 28 px.

prompts.label: Production
prompts.prompt:
Act as a social design lead building six headers for one campaign, each with the same dead-zone system.

Inputs [replace]: six post titles, one host portrait, palette forest #2F4A3C, paper #F2E9DA, ink #1F1B18; delivery 1500x500 PNG and 600x200 mobile proof.

Deliverables: six headers, one 1200x630 link-card crop, a dead-zone template, a mobile proof sheet at 600x200, and names post-version.

Design system: avatar zone left 150 px; name zone bottom 40 px; mobile center 600 px; logo 90 px; tagline 28 px minimum; one accent; type never over the portrait's face. A proof sheet at 1200x630 checks the same message on a link card.

Workflow: 1) intake titles and cut each to six words; 2) build the dead-zone template; 3) design header one as canary; 4) check at 600x200; 5) batch the other five; 6) review as a set; 7) run gates; 8) export with the template.

Gates: all six 1500x500; logo outside the avatar zone; tagline readable at 600x200; no title over six words; one accent per header; no face cropped.

No header exceeds six words.

Audit: the headers that broke the template, the mobile crop that failed, and the pair that looks the same.

Do not move the avatar zone per header; do not add a CTA the account cannot honor; do not crop the portrait at the eyes.

prompts.label: Edge / stress
prompts.prompt:
Act as a social designer stress-testing a header with a long tagline and a logo that must stay.

Inputs [replace]: 14-word tagline, square logo with fine type, photo with a bright sky behind the text area; palette forest #2F4A3C and paper #F2E9DA.

Deliverable: two 1500x500 options, one 600x200 mobile proof, a legibility report, and a note on the logo.

Design system: tagline 28 px minimum; safe area 60% of width.

Workflow: 1) measure available width outside the dead zones; 2) cut the tagline to two options; 3) test text on the bright sky; 4) add a scrim only if contrast fails; 5) check the logo at 90 px; 6) run gates; 7) export with the report.

Gates: tagline readable at 600x200; logo type not blurred at 90 px; contrast 4.5:1; no text under the avatar; exact 1500x500.

Audit: the words you cut, the contrast fix, and whether the logo needs a simplified version.

Exact 1500x500.

Do not put the tagline over the sky without a contrast fix; do not redraw the logo; do not shrink type below 24 px to fit.

title: Five posters a day means five decisions
description: A capped export budget rewards planning: one grid, one type scale, five poster variants, no wasted file.

prompts.label: Quick test
prompts.prompt:
Act as a print designer planning five poster variants when only five exports are available.

Inputs [replace]: event 'Night Market, Fri 18:00'; venue 'East Yard'; palette terracotta #B4553C, oat #E8DCCB, ink #1F1B18; one 3000 px hero photo.

Deliverable: five A3 297x420 mm PDFs at 300 dpi with 3 mm bleed, one contact sheet, and a variant log.

Design system: headline 42-64 pt; date and venue 18 pt minimum; 3 mm bleed; 5 mm safe margin; 12-column grid; one accent; 25 words maximum.

Workflow: 1) restate the event fields; 2) build one grid; 3) set three type sizes; 4) generate five variants with one variable each; 5) reject any variant that breaks the grid; 6) run gates; 7) export five files.

Gates: all five exact 297x420 mm; 3 mm bleed; date readable at 25%; no missing field; no watermark; one accent per poster.

Audit: the variant you rejected, the field that crowded the grid, and whether five exports were enough.

Do not spend an export on a variant that repeats another; do not add a sponsor; do not change the date.

prompts.label: Production
prompts.prompt:
Act as a print lead building a five-poster series for one week, with the same grid and a different daily message.

Inputs [replace]: five daily offers, venue, palette terracotta #B4553C, oat #E8DCCB, ink #1F1B18; A3 and A2 formats; 300 dpi.

Deliverables: five A3 PDFs and five A2 PDFs at 300 dpi with 3 mm bleed; five 1080x1528 social crops; a series grid; a daily copy sheet with the exact word count; names day-size-version.

Design system: headline 42-64 pt at A3, scaled 1.41x at A2; date and price 18 pt minimum; 3 mm bleed; 5 mm safe margin; one accent; 25 words maximum; same grid all week.

Workflow: 1) intake five offers and prices; 2) lock grid and type scale; 3) build day one as canary; 4) check at 25%; 5) produce days two to five; 6) compare the series; 7) run gates; 8) export both sizes.

Gates: all ten files 300 dpi with 3 mm bleed; prices exact; A2 scale exactly 1.41x; one accent per day; no layout drift; no poster over 25 words.

Each day keeps the same 12-column grid.

Audit: the day that broke the grid, the price that crowded, and the poster you would reprint.

Every file is checked at 100%. Do not change the grid mid-series; do not add a logo I did not supply; do not stretch A3 to A2.

prompts.label: Edge / stress
prompts.prompt:
Act as a print designer stress-testing a sixth poster when the daily export cap is already spent.

Inputs [replace]: five exports used, a sixth urgent poster for tomorrow, an existing A3 file that can be adapted; palette and grid locked.

Deliverable: one adapted A3 PDF at 297x420 mm from the existing file, a change list, and a cap note with the export count left.

Design system: 3 mm bleed; 5 mm safe margin; 18 pt minimum.

Workflow: 1) confirm the cap and the deadline; 2) list which existing file can carry the new message; 3) change copy only, not grid; 4) check the new date and price; 5) run gates; 6) export the adapted file; 7) write the cap note.

Gates: new copy exact; grid unchanged; 3 mm bleed intact; no leftover old date; no extra export used.

Audit: what you adapted, what you could not change, and whether tomorrow needs a new export.

18 pt date minimum.

Do not claim a new design when you adapted an old one; do not leave an old price; do not exceed the cap silently.

title: Five variants before one print run
description: A print run is the expensive part: generate and compare five headline routes at proof size before any press is booked.

prompts.label: Quick test
prompts.prompt:
Act as a print designer producing five A/B poster routes from one brief before a print run.

Inputs [replace]: event 'Open Studio, Sat 11:00-18:00'; venue 'Unit 4, Kiln St'; palette ink #1F1B18, oat #E8DCCB, terracotta #B4553C; 3000 px hero image.

Deliverable: five A3 PDFs at 300 dpi with 3 mm bleed, one proof sheet, and a pick rationale.

Design system: headline 48-72 pt; date and venue 16 pt minimum; 3 mm bleed; 5 mm safe margin; one grid; one accent; 20 words maximum.

Workflow: 1) restate the fields; 2) write five headline routes; 3) set one grid and three type sizes; 4) generate the five; 5) proof at 25%; 6) pick one and say why; 7) run gates; 8) export.

Gates: five files exact A3; 3 mm bleed; fields exact; headline readable at 25%; one accent; no route repeats another.

Audit: the routes rejected, the proof that failed at 25%, and the print risk you would flag.

Do not add a sponsor or price; do not change the date; do not pick by taste without a reason.

prompts.label: Production
prompts.prompt:
Act as an art director running a poster A/B system for a season of events, where every variant is print-ready.

Inputs [replace]: six events with dates and venues; palette ink #1F1B18, oat #E8DCCB, terracotta #B4553C; one hero image per event; A3 and A2.

Deliverables: six A3 PDFs at 300 dpi with 3 mm bleed, two A2 finals, a variant matrix listing the exact route per event, and names event-size-version.

Design system: headline 48-72 pt; secondary 16-20 pt; 3 mm bleed; 5 mm safe margin; 12-column grid; one accent; 20 words maximum; same grid all season.

Workflow: 1) intake six events; 2) lock grid and type scale; 3) write two headline routes per event; 4) build the matrix; 5) generate A3 first; 6) pick one route per event at 25%; 7) scale two winners to A2; 8) run gates; 9) export.

Gates: dates and venues exact; all files 300 dpi with 3 mm bleed; A2 scale 1.41x; no route over 20 words; one accent per poster; no layout drift.

Audit: the route that won and why, the event that needed a different grid, and the poster most likely to fail at print.

Every file 300 dpi with a 5 mm safe margin.

Do not print two routes for one event; do not stretch A3 to A2; do not add a logo I did not supply.

prompts.label: Edge / stress
prompts.prompt:
Act as a print designer stress-testing a poster when the headline is long and the print shop needs CMYK.

Inputs [replace]: 16-word headline, A2 at 300 dpi, print shop asks for CMYK PDF with 3 mm bleed; palette ink #1F1B18, oat #E8DCCB; one 1200 px photo.

Deliverable: one A2 CMYK PDF at 420x594 mm, one RGB proof, a limitation note, and a print checklist.

Design system: 3 mm bleed; 300 dpi; 5 mm safe margin.

Workflow: 1) audit headline length and photo resolution; 2) cut the headline to two options; 3) convert to CMYK and check color shift; 4) place the photo and mark its limit; 5) check bleed and safe margin; 6) run gates; 7) export with the note.

Gates: CMYK values recorded; bleed 3 mm; headline readable at 25%; photo not upscaled beyond 120%; no text in the safe margin.

Audit: the color that shifted, the photo limit, and whether the print shop should run a proof.

Do not convert without checking the black; do not upscale the photo silently; do not promise color match without a proof.

title: Design the 3000 px master for the 60 px thumbnail
description: The cover is judged at 60x60 in a queue: build the master so the title, the mark and the contrast survive the shrink.

prompts.label: Quick test
prompts.prompt:
Act as a cover designer producing one podcast cover that must read at 60x60 px.

Inputs [replace]: show 'The Long Way Home'; episode 'Ep. 12 - The ferry'; host 'Mara'; palette midnight #1B2A3A, sand #D8C3A5, coral #E0705A.

Deliverable: one 3000x3000 PNG at 300 dpi, one 60x60 proof, one 1400x1400 preview, and a legibility note.

Design system: title 240-320 px cap height at master; 60x60 test keeps at least two words; mark 300 px; contrast 4.5:1; safe margin 150 px; four words maximum.

Workflow: 1) cut the title to four words; 2) set type at master size; 3) place the mark; 4) shrink to 60x60 and check; 5) fix contrast or size if it fails; 6) run gates; 7) export three files.

Gates: title readable at 60x60; no text in the outer 150 px; contrast 4.5:1; exact 3000x3000; no guest photo without release.

Audit: the word that disappeared at 60 px, the contrast fix, and whether the title needs a shorter cut.

Do not put the episode number in the cover; do not use a photo without a release; do not add a fifth word.

prompts.label: Production
prompts.prompt:
Act as a cover art director building a twelve-episode season system, one master and eleven derived covers.

Inputs [replace]: show 'The Long Way Home'; twelve episode titles; one host portrait; palette midnight #1B2A3A, sand #D8C3A5, coral #E0705A; delivery 3000x3000 PNG at 300 dpi.

Deliverables: twelve covers at 3000x3000, a template file, a 60x60 proof sheet and one 1400x1400 preview each, and names episode-version.

Design system: title 240-320 px; episode strip 120 px; mark 300 px; safe margin 150 px; four words maximum; one accent; same template all season.

Workflow: 1) intake twelve titles and cut to four words; 2) lock template and type scale; 3) build episode one as canary; 4) check at 60x60 and 1400 px; 5) produce the remaining eleven; 6) review the season wall; 7) run gates; 8) export with the template.

Gates: all twelve 3000x3000; title readable at 60x60; no text in the outer 150 px; one accent per cover; no episode repeats another layout; no missing title.

Every file 300 dpi, four words maximum per title, one accent only.

Audit: the covers that failed at 60 px, the title that needed a shorter cut, and the pair that looks the same.

Every file is checked at 100%. Do not change the template mid-season; do not add a guest photo without a release; do not put two accents on one cover.

prompts.label: Edge / stress
prompts.prompt:
Act as a cover designer stress-testing a long show title on dark artwork.

Inputs [replace]: 8-word show title, dark illustration with low contrast, no logo file, delivery 3000x3000 PNG.

Deliverable: two cover options, one 60x60 proof each, a contrast report with the measured ratio, and a note on the missing logo.

Design system: 3000x3000 master; 150 px outer margin; no type below 600 weight.

Workflow: 1) cut the title to two options of four words; 2) test light and dark type on the artwork; 3) add a plate only if contrast fails; 4) check at 60x60; 5) keep the option that reads; 6) run gates; 7) export with the report.

Gates: title readable at 60x60; contrast 4.5:1; no text in the outer 150 px; exact 3000x3000; no drawn logo.

Audit: the word you cut, the contrast fix, and whether the show needs a logo before launch.

300 dpi export, 60x60 proof.

Do not invent a logo; do not put the title on a busy area without a plate; do not use a font lighter than 600 weight at 60 px.
